plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden faces that follow the sun across the sky. Fields of them glow like sunlit seas, and bees crowd the dark, seed-filled centers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Great Plains of North America and farmland across Europe, including France and Ukraine
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower. It is a cluster of hundreds or even thousands of tiny florets. Young buds track the sun from east to west each day.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Moorlands turn into rolling carpets of purple as tiny bell-shaped blooms open across the hills. The honey-sweet scent hums with bees on warm late-summer afternoons.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late July to September or October
plants.location: Highland moors and heathlands of Scotland and northern England
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its thick, jelly-like texture. Beekeepers sometimes carry their hives onto the moors in late summer to catch the bloom.

plants.name: Liatris spicata
plants.description: Tall, feathery spires of fluffy purple flowers rise from grassy clumps. Unusually, the blooms open from the top of the spike downward. Monarch butterflies flock to them in late summer.
plants.location: Prairies, meadows and moist grasslands of eastern and central North America
plants.funFact: Most spiked flowers open from the bottom up. Blazing star reverses the order, which gives each spike a fuzzy, torch-like look.
